task1.title: Cars per 1000 people in five European countries
task1.prompt: The bar chart shows the number of cars per 1000 people in 5 European countries in 3 years and compares with the European average.

chartDesc.title: The number of cars per 1000 people in 5 countries and the average
chartDesc.overview: Country 5 had the highest number of cars per 1000 people across all three years, while Country 1 consistently recorded the lowest figure. Country 4 remained completely unchanged throughout the period.
unreadable: Exact numerical values above bars are not printed; figures are visually read based on y-axis gridlines.
keyFeatures: Country 5 was the highest in all years, peaking at around 975 cars per 1000 people in 2015.
Country 1 was the lowest overall, standing at 300 in 2005, rising to 400 in 2009, and returning to 300 in 2015.
Country 4 remained constant at approximately 685 cars per 1000 people in 2005, 2009, and 2015.
The average of 5 stood at 690 in 2005, dropped slightly to 660 in 2009, and rose to 770 in 2015.

task1.instruction: Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
task1.sampleBand8:
The bar chart shows how many cars there were for every 1,000 people in five European countries in 2005, 2009 and 2015, alongside the average for the five.

Overall, car ownership varied widely between the countries, and the trends over time were far from uniform: some nations saw steady growth while others fluctuated or barely changed. Country 5 had the most cars throughout, whereas Country 1 consistently had the fewest.

Country 5 stood out as the most car-dependent nation, its figure rising from just under 900 vehicles per 1,000 people in 2005 to almost 1,000 by 2015, well above the group average in every year. Country 1, by contrast, had the lowest ownership: after climbing from around 300 to 400 between 2005 and 2009, it fell back to its original level of 300 in 2015, the only country to end below where it began.

The middle three countries clustered more closely. Country 4's figure was remarkably stable at about 680 in all three years, while Country 3 edged down slightly from roughly 690 to 580 and Country 2 hovered around 500. The five-country average mirrored this mixed picture, dipping from about 690 in 2005 to 660 in 2009 before rebounding to 770 in 2015.

Ustunli diagramma besh Yevropa mamlakatida 2005, 2009 va 2015-yillarda har 1 000 kishiga qancha avtomobil to'g'ri kelganini hamda besh mamlakat o'rtacha ko'rsatkichini aks ettiradi.

Umuman olganda, avtomobil egaligi mamlakatlar o'rtasida keng miqyosda farq qilgan va vaqt o'tishidagi tendensiyalar bir xil bo'lishdan yiroq edi: ba'zi davlatlarda barqaror o'sish kuzatilgan bo'lsa, boshqalarida ko'rsatkich tebrangan yoki deyarli o'zgarmagan. 5-mamlakatda boshdan-oxir eng ko'p avtomobil bo'lgan, 1-mamlakatda esa doimiy ravishda eng kam.

5-mamlakat eng avtomobilga qaram davlat sifatida ajralib turdi: uning ko'rsatkichi 2005-yildagi har 1 000 kishiga 900 taga yaqin avtomobildan 2015-yilga kelib deyarli 1 000 taga ko'tarildi — bu har yili guruh o'rtachasidan ancha yuqori. 1-mamlakatda esa aksincha, egalik eng past edi: 2005–2009-yillarda taxminan 300 dan 400 ga ko'tarilgach, 2015-yilda dastlabki 300 darajasiga qaytib tushdi — bu boshlangan nuqtasidan pastroqda yakunlagan yagona mamlakat.

O'rtadagi uch mamlakat bir-biriga yaqinroq to'plandi. 4-mamlakat ko'rsatkichi har uch yilda ham taxminan 680 da hayratlanarli darajada barqaror bo'ldi, 3-mamlakat esa taxminan 690 dan 580 ga bir oz pastladi, 2-mamlakat 500 atrofida turdi. Besh mamlakat o'rtachasi bu aralash manzarani aks ettirdi: 2005-yildagi taxminan 690 dan 2009-yilda 660 ga tushib, so'ng 2015-yilda 770 ga qayta ko'tarildi.

task2.title: How should a country's success be measured?
task2.prompt: Economic progress is often used to measure a country's success. However, some people believe that other factors are more important. What other factors should be considered when measuring a country's success? Do you think one factor is more important than the others?
task2.instruction: Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
task2.sampleBand8:
The wealth of a nation, usually measured by economic output, is often treated as the clearest sign of its success. In reality, however, prosperity is only one dimension of a country's wellbeing, and I believe several other factors deserve equal attention, with quality of life ultimately mattering most.

Money undeniably matters, since economic growth funds hospitals, schools and infrastructure. Yet a high income tells us nothing about how that wealth is shared or experienced, which is why other measures are essential. The first is the health and education of the population: a country where people live long, well-educated lives is clearly succeeding, whatever its bank balance. A second is social equality — a nation whose riches reach only a tiny elite, leaving millions in poverty, can hardly be called successful. Equally important are political freedom and safety, since citizens who enjoy the rule of law and can speak without fear are better off than wealthy people living under repression. Finally, environmental sustainability now belongs on any honest scorecard, because growth achieved by poisoning the air and exhausting natural resources simply borrows from the future.

Although all these factors count, I do consider one more important than the rest: the overall wellbeing of ordinary citizens. Wealth, health, freedom and a clean environment are, in the end, valuable precisely because they allow people to lead safe, healthy and fulfilling lives. A country that delivers this for the majority is genuinely successful, whereas one that tops the economic tables while its people remain unhappy has, in my view, missed the point.

In conclusion, economic strength is important but far from sufficient. Health, equality, freedom and environmental care must all be weighed, and the truest measure of success is whether a country's people can flourish.
task2.uzSampleBand8:
Mamlakat boyligi, odatda iqtisodiy ishlab chiqarish bilan o'lchanadigan, ko'pincha uning muvaffaqiyatining eng aniq belgisi deb qaraladi. Ammo aslida farovonlik mamlakat baxt-saodatining atigi bitta o'lchovidir va menimcha, bir qancha boshqa omillar ham teng e'tiborga loyiq, hayot sifati esa oxir-oqibat eng muhimidir.

Pul, shubhasiz, ahamiyatli, chunki iqtisodiy o'sish kasalxonalar, maktablar va infratuzilmani moliyalashtiradi. Biroq yuqori daromad o'sha boylik qanday taqsimlangani yoki his qilingani haqida hech narsa aytmaydi — shu bois boshqa o'lchovlar zarur. Birinchisi — aholining sog'lig'i va ta'limi: odamlar uzoq va yaxshi ma'lumotli hayot kechiradigan mamlakat, bank hisobidan qat'i nazar, yaqqol muvaffaqiyatga erishmoqda. Ikkinchisi — ijtimoiy tenglik: boyligi faqat kichik bir tabaqaga yetib, millionlab odamni qashshoqlikda qoldiradigan davlatni muvaffaqiyatli deb bo'lmaydi. Shu qadar muhimi — siyosiy erkinlik va xavfsizlik, chunki qonun ustuvorligidan bahramand bo'lgan va qo'rquvsiz gapira oladigan fuqarolar zulm ostida yashayotgan badavlat odamlardan ko'ra yaxshiroq ahvolda. Nihoyat, ekologik barqarorlik ham endi har qanday halol baholash mezoniga kiradi, chunki havoni zaharlab va tabiiy resurslarni tugatib erishilgan o'sish shunchaki kelajakdan qarz oladi.

Bu omillarning barchasi muhim bo'lsa-da, men bittasini qolganlaridan muhimroq deb bilaman: oddiy fuqarolarning umumiy farovonligi. Boylik, salomatlik, erkinlik va toza atrof-muhit, pirovardida, aynan odamlarga xavfsiz, sog'lom va mazmunli hayot kechirish imkonini bergani uchun qadrlidir. Buni ko'pchilik uchun ta'minlaydigan mamlakat chinakam muvaffaqiyatlidir, xalqi baxtsiz qolgani holda iqtisodiy jadvallarda birinchi o'rinni egallagan mamlakat esa, menimcha, asosiy mohiyatni chetlab o'tgan.

Xulosa qilib aytganda, iqtisodiy qudrat muhim, biroq yetarli emas. Salomatlik, tenglik, erkinlik va atrof-muhitga g'amxo'rlik — barchasi tarozida o'lchanishi kerak, muvaffaqiyatning eng haqqoniy mezoni esa mamlakat xalqi gullab-yashnay oladimi yoki yo'qmi degan savoldir.
